synthesis.item: Pastor and leader (pastor_leader) — Futures Daily Word
synthesis.angle: A man who feeds everyone and is fed by no one opens the app at 6am with Sunday already leaning on him. Two things are true at once — he needs God, and he needs a sermon — and the app currently makes him meet them in the wrong order, then shows him a number it made up. This design fixes the order, never lets the work disappear while it waits its turn, and refuses to print a figure it cannot count.
synthesis.thesis: His own reading comes first, his work comes second and is never more than one tap away, the app never pretends to be his ghostwriter, and every number it shows him is real. Today the greeting says "This is your time — not ministry, just you and God" (persona-config.ts:253) and then three things contradict it: the Preach card renders above the hero (HomeScreen.tsx:2106, comment "just below the greeting, always visible"), all fifteen Between You & God prompts are about his staff, his vision and his church (persona-config.ts:473-489), and the Sunday card prints a days-read figure computed as Math.min(streak, 7) (HomeScreen.tsx:115) from a streak that increments on Home mount (HomeScreen.tsx:787) — it counts opens, not reading. Meanwhile the pastor-only "To sermon" action files verses into dw_sermon_prep whose only display lives in an unmounted export (SermonWorkspace.tsx:62; App.tsx mounts only SermonNotesTab). Nothing here is removed and nothing is stripped: the fix is order, honesty and giving his filed work a home.
principles: Feed the man before you serve the pastor. The reading and Between You & God sit above anything that leaves the app for Sunday — which is also the standing ruling (Sermon Notes row demoted below the reading for pastor_leader, PR #82).
Never take the work away, only move it down. He came for a sermon too. Preach stays on Home, one tap, carrying a count of what is waiting.

Never show a pastor a number the app made up. Campus Overview already refuses to fabricate; the habit surfaces must meet the same standard or the whole trust panel is theatre. Count filed passages and real read-days; never estimate minutes saved.

The AI thinks with him; it does not write for him and it does not quote what it has not checked. 79% of pastors worry AI could replace God's role, 63% pastoral leadership, 71% are cautious (Barna/Gloo, Dec 2025, n=442).
Show the source on the surface, not in Settings. The study layer is already public-domain and CC (study.js); reviewers document AI tools fabricating cross-references on less-common passages.
Presence over problem-solving. Between You & God asks; it does not diagnose, prescribe or graduate him.
Depth stays open for this persona. The clutter complaint is Persona 3's, not his — his ranked needs are research speed, original languages and trustworthy sourcing.
Nothing on this path shames him. No streak threat, no 'you missed a day', no notification implying he let God down.
Crisis is not a persona anyone picks on a good day — least of all a pastor. Comfort must be reachable from his path without changing his path.
Richer, warmer, editorial. Photo hero, white paper reading panel in both themes, terracotta and ivory, Georgia serif, no italics. Nothing greyed, nothing deleted.

journey.day0: He arrives one of two ways. Either he taps the path swatch or the landing line and picks "I'm a pastor and I teach and preach" in the one sheet, which saves as a real choice (source 'settings' or 'onboarding') and navigates straight to Home; or he signs in with his work email in More and the boot restore stamps pastor_leader — only when dw_setup is absent or auto-sourced — and provisions his campus code through my-campus-code. Home opens with today's chapter already open, seeded credit-free, bypassing handleRead. Commentary is expanded with its source printed. Between You & God sits under it. With no plan the hero serves the PASTOR_CHAPTERS leadership rotation so the screen is never blank, with one new line saying what the rotation is and that a dated plan is a tap away. Nothing blocks him: not the wizard, not sign-in, not email.
journey.first_session: He reads. He is asked for nothing. Under the reading, Between You & God asks him one question about himself rather than about his staff, with Journal this / Talk it through and a privacy line — verified before it ships. Under that, one quiet comfort line. Then commentary with its licence. Then the study assistant with its four prompts and one honest line about what it will and will not do. Then Preach — the only thing that leaves the app, now sitting under his own reading rather than over it, with the congregation label gone from its sub-line. If he highlights a verse, "To sermon" files it and the Preach card's sub-line changes to name the count. Mark as read credits the day, records the streak once, and writes the new dw_read_days ledger. The push ask comes after that first finished reading, never stacked with the path question.
journey.return_visit: Same screen, same order, nothing re-explained. If he started a plan, Today's Study replaces the rotation with the Greek/Hebrew toggle on the passage. The Preach card carries the running count of what he filed; tapping the count opens the filed sheet, where he can copy it all out, edit what he is preaching through, and remove anything. The reflection prompt has rotated. The greeting bands on real read-days from the ledger, not on opens — so a pastor who only opened the app is never congratulated for reading.
journey.week2: He has a rhythm or he does not, and the app treats both the same. His filed bag has real weight now, which is the moment Copy all earns itself and the outline prompt has his own material to shape. The hero eyebrow reads PREACHING · {focus} once a focus is set. On Sunday, Your week appears with two now-truthful tiles, one line about what he gathered, and one question written for a pastor rather than a congregant. By now he has seen the source line under commentary and the check line under every AI answer; if the trust work lands, session length goes up and the event will say so.
journey.missed_day: Nothing turns red. The single freeze in streak.ts:63-79 bridges one missed day; it now says so once, plainly — "You missed a day. The streak held." — instead of spending silently, and that line is only honest because the ledger records reading rather than opens. Past two days the count resets quietly and the greeting reads "You're back. Nothing to make up." No catch-up prompt, no make-up reading, no re-onboarding, no 'you were doing so well'. Guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall, and a pastor already carries a professional obligation to be devout — the app must not add to it. The filed bag still shows everything, so no work looks lost.
journey.seasonal: Advent, Lent, Easter and a Futures series are the spikes (YouVersion 21.6M opens on Easter 2026; Hallow 300% subscription growth in Lent). For every other persona the seasonal read is something they join; for the pastor it is something he starts for his campus, and the estate already has the mechanism in /staff intake with its approval chain. His own recurring calendar moment is not Easter — it is Sunday, every week, forever, plus whatever series he is preaching, which dw_sermon_prep_focus already holds. For the first two weeks he sees only the reader's side: a church-wide read line in the For Sunday card and a plan he can start. Whether a campus pastor can launch a campus-wide read from inside Daily Word is an owner decision, not something to build into this pass.

synthesis.comfort_access: One quiet line at the foot of Between You & God — "Heavy week? Open the comfort readings. Your path stays where it is." — plus the same entry from Bible AI's empty state. It opens the comfort surface as a sub-view over his own path, on useSubView ALONE, never useSubView plus useModalA11y or aria-modal, because nested focus traps have already cost this app a working Android back button and a keyboard-unreachable overlay. Inside it: one passage, slow audio first, low stimulus, the comfortMode toolbar restricted to Note and Close only, no streak, no count, no 'complete', and no 'Feeling Stronger?' graduation prompt, ever. It must NOT call saveSetup — his saved path stays pastor_leader, his plan, his filed bag and his campus tools are all untouched, and closing returns him to pastor Home exactly where he left. It is worded as a place, not a condition, because a check-in question is exactly what a pastor will refuse. This matters more for this persona than any other: 38% of pastors considered quitting in the past year and 65% report loneliness, up from 42% in 2015. Separately, if crisis language appears in what he types into Bible AI or a prayer request, the safety panel takes over the answer area: presence first, then the region-correct line matched to his campus (988 in the US, 13 11 14 in Australia, 0800 543 354 in New Zealand), then the first-use disclosure that this is scripture and a church rather than counselling, then Keep reading / I'm okay. It never stacks with another gate and never re-triggers in the same session for the same message. The keyword matcher needs a false-positive suite of biblical phrasing before it ships — 'the death of Christ', 'dying to self' and 'I'm dying to preach this' must not fire; 'I don't want to be here any more' must. Which lines per congregation, and who at each campus receives a pastor's own prayer request — including whether it routes to a peer rather than to the campus he leads — are Ashley's calls.
synthesis.reminders: One a day, at the hour he actually opens, worded neutrally, and never about the streak. The machinery already exists — a stored preferred_hour per subscriber, an hourly cron with a two-hour catch-up window and a once-per-local-day ledger — so this is a copy and timing change, not new plumbing. The new dw_read_days ledger stores the local date and hour of each REAL completion for the last 14 days; after five to seven sessions the reminder hour picker in More defaults to his modal hour and the card says so in one line. That is Duolingo's behaviour-inferred timing, which the research names as the pattern to copy. Copy is verse-first and neutral — "Your chapter is open. 1 Peter 5." or "Ten minutes before the day starts." After a missed day the message acknowledges the gap and offers today with no accounting: "Yesterday got away. Today's chapter is open." Never 'don't lose your streak', never 'you missed yesterday'. Guilt-framed reminders drive opt-out and uninstall, and a pastor already carries a professional obligation to be devout; the app must not add to it, and opt-out is a permanent loss of the only channel we have. Three live constraints hold: the ask fires only after the first completed reading and never stacks with PathAskedOnce; templates and verse snippets live hardcoded in netlify/functions/push-send.js with EN and ID only, so es/pt must be added there — or better, moved out of the function entirely so wording and a new language never need a deploy; and pushSupported() allowlists futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost only, so none of this is verifiable on a deploy preview or the futures.church proxy. Verify on prod or localhost, and read the delivered text per language. The grace side stays in streak.ts exactly as it is — one freeze, replenished after seven days, the count bridged rather than reset — with the single change that the app now SAYS so once when it happens. No new freeze rules. Two pastor-specific questions are his to settle and ship as switches rather than assumptions: whether push is suppressed on Sunday morning while he is working, and whether Sunday opens are excluded when inferring his hour.
instrumentation: One dw_events table and one nightly rollup by path and cohort week. This is build item one in the research and everything else here is unreadable without it. TRACKED_EVENTS (src/utils/analytics.ts:31-38) is a hardcoded allowlist containing no pastor events at all — anything not listed is silently dropped, so the client allowlist entry and the call site must ship in the same commit, with a test that fails when they diverge.

Whether the Sunday card stays on Sunday or moves to Monday. Sunday is his heaviest working morning and a preaching pastor may never see the card; the ruling pins it pastor-only, not to a day. The event will say so within a month — do not defend it if it does not.

Which crisis lines show for which congregation (US, AU, NZ drafted), and whether a pastor's own safety moment ever notifies a human. If it does, who — the person a campus pastor would actually accept hearing from, which is probably not the campus he leads.

Whether the filed captures bag stays a Daily Word sheet or moves wholesale into Pastors Sermon Prep. Two apps holding the same bag is how they end up disagreeing; the Copy all event will tell you which way to go.
Whether PreachScreen.tsx and src/components/preach/* are deleted now or parked. There is a working OutlineBuilder with a 4D/H.E.A.T. picker in there that nothing can reach.
Whether push is suppressed for pastors on Sunday morning, and whether Sunday opens are excluded when inferring his reminder hour. Both plausible, both unsourced — ship them as switches and test.

Whether the Campus Overview prayer number becomes a list he can act on or stays a count. A number he cannot reach is a scoreboard; a list is pastoral care. That is a data-access decision, not a design one.
Who may edit public/books/pastor-study.json — Ashley only, or campus pastors through the staff site. That decides whether it is a file he owns or an intake surface.

Whether a campus pastor may set a campus reading, and whether the pastor tier is priced flat. The research flags real backlash against recurring cost in this market; nothing in this design depends on the answer.
risks: The Preach move reorders the opening screen. Owner-preview-gated by ruling — ship it behind a preview link and do not merge on anyone's word but his. This is the class of change that got PR #80 reverted with 'you have completely stripped, go back'.

If the Preach card moves and path_arrival_pastor does not — in all four languages — the app lies to a pastor in the first sentence he reads on the new layout. It currently says 'Preach is the card above'.

dw_read_days is a new synced key. It must merge into what is currently in localStorage and touch only its own field, never be rebuilt from React state, and it rides the misc bag fill-only with pushNow on write. A stale mount-time rebuild of a synced dw_* record has already destroyed nine days of a reader's progress across devices.

‼️ Do not delete SermonWorkspace.tsx. App.tsx:92 imports SermonNotesTab from it, which is the congregation Sermon Notes destination. Only the unmounted SermonWorkspace export and PreachScreen + preach/* go.

'Only you can see this. Nobody at the church does.' must be PROVEN before it ships — grep netlify/functions/user-sync.js and pastor-admin.js for any staff-facing read path that touches journal content. If it cannot be proven, the line comes out. An overstated privacy promise to a pastor is worse than no promise.

The filed sheet is a subview-driven card: it must stay MOUNTED with a live open prop and use useSubView alone, never useSubView plus useModalA11y or aria-modal. Both traps have already cost this app a working Android back button and a keyboard-unreachable overlay.
pastor_preach_exit fires on a navigation away from the PWA. Without sendBeacon it will never arrive, and the one number that settles the demotion will read zero.

New event types need BOTH the client allowlist and the dashboard aggregation. Adding one without the other silently drops the data, and the whole instrumentation build reads as working while recording nothing. The server aggregate must also tolerate event types it does not know.

Moving prompts and chapters into /books hits the service-worker cache trap. /books/* is network-first now, but CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION must move together for any sw.js change, and returning readers see the change on the SECOND open after deploy, not the first.
Touching pastor_leader's sectionOrder in persona-config.ts risks the tests that pin the other four personas. Change one persona's array per commit and run the whole suite, not the pastor specs alone.
Deploy previews return 403 from the app's own /api, so scripture falls back to offline KJV and push does not exist there. Verify translations, study sources and reminders on PROD, not on the preview.

Push copy lives in a Netlify function with no CMS, so every wording change is a deploy until it moves out — and none of it is verifiable on a preview or the futures.church proxy, only localhost or prod.
The crisis keyword matcher will produce false positives on scripture. It needs a test suite of biblical phrasing before it goes anywhere near a pastor's screen.
Two milestone lists already exist — one in streak.ts, one in the greeting section — and they are out of sync. Do not add a third; if the prep line needs a threshold, read the existing one.
Every new string needs en/es/pt/id or t() renders the raw key on screen, and translated content is Claude-drafted then approved before ship.
Sermon frameworks stay 4D and H.E.A.T. only. Nothing in this design names a framework, and nothing added later should invent one.
